articles.title: ‘We want our story to be told’: inside a shocking 36-year fight for justice in Baltimore
articles.summary: A staggering case of injustice is explored in the galling HBO documentary When a Witness Recants. The three subjects and producer Ta-Nehisi Coates explain how it unfolded For most of his life, the writer Ta-Nehisi Coates would occasionally think of a chilling episode from his childhood in West Baltimore: almost exactly 43 years ago, on 18 November 1983, a 14-year-old boy named DeWitt Duckett was shot and killed in a hallway of Harlem Park junior high school in the middle of the afternoon, by an older teenager who stole his blue satin Georgetown jacket. Coates was only eight years old at the time, too young to know the details, but old enough to perceive the collective horror around him. articles.title: ‘I hope paramedics are on standby for the sex scenes!’ The wet and wild TV experience leaving fans dizzy
articles.summary: From icy squirts to bed-bouncing vibrations, erotic hockey drama Heated Rivalry just got even raunchier in ‘extreme sensory’ 4DX cinema screenings. But one scene proved too much – even for the super fans I’m in the cinema foyer when I first spot them: hockey jerseys. Lots of them. “I’ve no idea what to expect!” giggles Chloe, who is wearing a black and yellow “Rozanov” jersey. Like me, she has never been to a 4DX screening before – but when Cineworld announced it would be showing episodes five and six of queer hockey drama Heated Rivalry in the novel format, she booked tickets immediately. “I actually had tickets for the 2D screening, but cancelled them for this,” she says. articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love story
articles.summary: With realism that defies belief, this vast game easily accommodates its trademark foulmouthed, OTT chaos – as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre In GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen. Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start. If you had been spying on me playing this game over the past few weeks you may well have caught me robbing banks, shooting up a weed farm or tearing along the highway at sunset blaring Bad Bunny on the in-game radio, but you might equally have caught me doing squats at the gym, shopping, assembling a coffee table or walking along the beach eating ice-cream. articles.title: ‘Everything he said sounded like a song title!’ The rackety, romantic life of Bobby Charles, alligator-befriending bard of the bayou
articles.summary: He was nearly an early rock’n’roll star but took a different path, from Fats Domino to the Band and pro-environment songwriting. As a career-spanning box set is released, those who knew him remember an American original ‘I was listening to Bob Dylan’s Theme Time radio show,” says Korey Richey, multi-instrumentalist with LCD Soundsystem, “and he said, ‘Bobby Charles is best known as a songwriter, but he has one of the most melodious voices ever transmuted into a piece of vinyl.’ I thought about it, and I agree: Bobby Charles was something else.” Something else, indeed. Charles (1938–2010) was unable to play an instrument yet wrote songs sung by everyone from Fats Domino to Etta James to Kris Kristofferson.
